title: Progress-Test Revision: Sport, Questions and Future Plans
subtitle: A2+/B1 revision practice for sports, competition language, questions and future forms.
lessonNotes: This is revision for the next progress test: listening, grammar, vocabulary and reading.
Review sports and active-lifestyle words, then use competition language such as fair chance, compete, qualify and succeed.
Make questions carefully: use do/does for Present Simple and am/is/are for Present Continuous.
Use will for a decision or promise made now. Use be going to for an existing intention or plan.
Use Present Simple for a timetable or routine, but Present Continuous for an arrangement that is already fixed: The match starts at six; we are meeting at five.
Notice useful verb patterns: succeed in + verb-ing, decide to + base verb, and look forward to + noun or verb-ing.
When you answer a question, give a complete idea when possible: Yes, I do because it helps me relax. This makes your speaking sound clearer.

grammar.title: Present Simple and Present Continuous
grammar.rule: Use Present Simple for routines and facts. Use Present Continuous for an action happening now or around now.
examples: They are climbing at the sports centre now.
What does he watch after school?

grammar.title: Question formation
grammar.rule: Choose the auxiliary that matches the tense, then put the subject after it.
examples: What does your sister love watching?
Why are the players practising today?
Where do you usually go surfing?

grammar.title: Will and be going to
grammar.rule: Use will for a quick decision or promise. Use be going to for an intention that already exists.
examples: I will call you after the match.
We are going to practise for the progress test.
I will not show off, I promise.

grammar.title: Present Continuous for arrangements
grammar.rule: Use Present Continuous for a personal future arrangement when the time, place or people are already organised.
examples: I am meeting Sam at the pool on Friday.
Are they travelling to the tournament tomorrow?
We are not playing after school today.

grammar.title: Useful verb patterns
grammar.rule: Some verbs need a particular form after them. Learn the complete pattern, not only the new word.
examples: Lina succeeded in finishing the route.
The team decided to practise indoors.
I am looking forward to watching the final.

vocabulary.meaning: the sport of riding and doing tricks on a skateboard
vocabulary.example: Skateboarding is part of many international events.
Clear rules give every player a fair chance.

vocabulary.meaning: to take part in a competition
vocabulary.example: Teams compete to reach the final.

vocabulary.meaning: to reach the standard needed to join an event
vocabulary.example: Only the best runners qualify for the next round.

vocabulary.meaning: to achieve what you try to do
vocabulary.example: She succeeded in finishing the climbing course.

vocabulary.meaning: to change something so it suits a new situation
vocabulary.example: The club adapted the rules for younger players.

vocabulary.meaning: to give someone an idea or wish to do something
vocabulary.example: The athlete inspires young people to get active.

vocabulary.meaning: to try to make people notice your skill or success
vocabulary.example: He can show off his skateboard skills at the park.

vocabulary.meaning: a person who watches a sport or event
vocabulary.example: The spectators cheered when the final started.

vocabulary.meaning: the objects needed for an activity
vocabulary.example: You do not need expensive equipment to go jogging.

vocabulary.meaning: to join an activity or event
vocabulary.example: More than forty students are taking part in the race.

vocabulary.meaning: to become better, or make something better
vocabulary.example: Regular practice can improve your balance.

vocabulary.meaning: something difficult that tests your ability
vocabulary.example: The climbing wall is a fun challenge for beginners.

practice.q: Choose the correct question about a routine.
opt: What does Mia do after school?
What is Mia do after school?
What do Mia does after school?
practice.a: What does Mia do after school?
practice.why: Use does + the base verb for a Present Simple question with she/he/it.

practice.q: Choose the correct question about an action now.
opt: Why the players are practising now?
Why are the players practising now?
Why do the players practising now?
practice.a: Why are the players practising now?
practice.why: Use are + subject + verb-ing for Present Continuous.

practice.q: You decide now to help your teammate. Choose the natural sentence.
opt: I am going to help you now.
practice.why: Will can show a decision made at the moment of speaking.

practice.q: Choose the sentence about a plan that already exists.
opt: We are going to practise for the test tonight.
We will to practise for the test tonight.
We going to practise for the test tonight.
practice.a: We are going to practise for the test tonight.
practice.why: Use be going to for an existing intention or plan.

opt: Every team deserves a fair chance.
Every team deserves a fair change.
Every team deserves fair chance to.
practice.a: Every team deserves a fair chance.
practice.why: A fair chance means an equal opportunity.

opt: She succeeded to win the race.
She succeeded in winning the race.
She succeeded at win the race.
practice.a: She succeeded in winning the race.

practice.q: The tickets are booked and the group has arranged a time. Choose the best sentence.
opt: We meet the coach at ten tomorrow.
We are meeting the coach at ten tomorrow.
We will meeting the coach at ten tomorrow.
practice.a: We are meeting the coach at ten tomorrow.
practice.why: Present Continuous can describe an organised personal arrangement.

practice.q: Choose the correct question word order.
opt: Where you are going to practise?
Where are you going to practise?
Where do you going to practise?
practice.a: Where are you going to practise?
practice.why: Put the auxiliary are before the subject: Where are you...?

practice.q: Choose the sentence with the correct meaning of take part.
opt: Ravi is watching the race from home.
Ravi is joining the race as a runner.
Ravi is repairing the race track.
practice.a: Ravi is joining the race as a runner.
practice.why: Take part means join an activity or event.

practice.q: Choose the best completion: The coach wants to ____ the warm-up for beginners.
practice.why: Adapt means change something so it suits a new situation.

reading.title: A New Olympic Challenge
reading.text:
At a city skate park, teenagers practise jumps and turns after school. Some of them enjoy showing off their skills, but they also help new skaters. The local club has adapted its beginner sessions so that younger children can join safely. For many visitors, skateboarding is more than a sport: it can inspire people to be active and try something new. This Saturday, the club is also offering a free equipment check, because helmets and boards need to be safe before anyone practises difficult moves.

Next month, the club is holding a small competition. The organisers want every skater to have a fair chance, so the rules are clear and the judges will explain their decisions. Only three skaters will qualify for the final. Lina is going to enter because she has trained for weeks. Her friend says, “I will come and support you.” Lina hopes to succeed, but she knows that enjoying the event matters too. After the final, the club is meeting to decide which activities it will offer in winter.

questions.q: Why did the club adapt its beginner sessions?
opt: To make them safer for younger children
To stop visitors using the park
questions.a: To make them safer for younger children
questions.why: The first paragraph gives this reason.

questions.q: What does the competition aim to give every skater?
Why is Lina going to enter?
questions.why: This is an existing intention supported by preparation.
The friend makes a promise with will.

questions.q: Why is the club offering an equipment check?
opt: To make sure equipment is safe
questions.a: To make sure equipment is safe
questions.why: The text links the check with safe practice.

questions.q: How many skaters will reach the final?
questions.why: The second paragraph gives the number.

questions.q: What are club members doing after the final?
questions.why: This is their arranged future meeting.

listening.title: Preparing for the Competition
listening.instructions: Listen twice. First, listen for the plan. Then listen again for grammar, competition vocabulary and the speakers’ reasons.
listening.script:
Noah: Are you doing anything after school, Ava?
Ava: Yes, I am going to practise climbing. Our club is preparing for a competition.
Noah: Do you compete often?
Ava: Not usually. This is my first event, but I hope I will qualify for the final.
Noah: I will come and watch.
Ava: Thanks. The coaches are giving every climber a fair chance, so I feel calmer.
Noah: Great. Do not show off too much!
Ava: I will not. I just want to enjoy it and succeed in finishing the route.
Noah: Are you meeting the team before the event?
Ava: Yes, we are meeting at the sports centre at nine. We are going to check our equipment together.
Noah: That sounds organised. I think you will do well.

questions.q: What is Ava going to practise?

opt: She is preparing for a competition
questions.a: She is preparing for a competition
questions.why: The club is preparing for an event.

questions.q: What does Ava want to succeed in doing?

opt: The coaches are treating climbers fairly
questions.a: The coaches are treating climbers fairly
questions.why: Ava says the coaches are giving every climber a fair chance.

questions.q: When are Ava and the team meeting?
opt: At nine at the sports centre
questions.a: At nine at the sports centre
questions.why: Ava gives both the time and the place.

questions.q: What are they going to do together?

topics.title: 1. A first competition
topics.prompt: Write 80–110 words about a fictional person preparing for their first sport or active-lifestyle competition. Include what they usually do, what they are doing now, one question they ask, one plan with be going to, and one promise with will. Use at least three unit words such as compete, fair chance, qualify, succeed, inspire, adapt or show off.

topics.title: 2. A club event invitation
topics.prompt: Write an 80–110 word invitation from a fictional sports club to a beginner event. Explain the activity, time and place, what equipment people need, and why everyone has a fair chance. Include one Present Continuous arrangement, one question, and a sentence with will.

topics.title: 3. A teammate’s plan
topics.prompt: Write 80–110 words about a fictional teammate's plan for the next month. Explain one routine, one current action, an intention with be going to, and something you promise to do. Use succeed in + verb-ing or decide to + verb.

topics.title: 4. A healthy challenge
topics.prompt: Write 80–110 words about a fictional 14-day healthy challenge. Describe the activities, a challenge the person expects, and how they will improve. Include one well-formed question and at least three words from the unit.

topics.title: 5. A fair competition report
topics.prompt: Write 80–110 words about a fictional school competition after it finishes. Say who took part, how the organisers gave everyone a fair chance, and what the writer is going to do next. Include one sentence with will and one Present Continuous arrangement.

checklist: Choose one topic and use a fictional name
Use Present Simple for a routine or fact
Use Present Continuous for an action now or an arrangement
Use be going to for a plan
Use will for a promise or decision
Use at least three unit words
Check verb patterns such as succeed in + verb-ing
Organise the writing into clear sentences
Read your work once and correct spelling or punctuation
